Kamasu

Dive · 41.8mm · 200m · automatic · 2016–2019

A family of popular and affordable mechanical dive watches, the Kamasu is defined by its aggressive, barracuda-inspired hands and indices, and the inclusion of a sapphire crystal as a standard feature.

The story

The Kamasu was introduced in the late 2010s, elevating Orient's entry-level diver offerings with the significant upgrade of a sapphire crystal over its predecessors, the Mako and Ray. The first generation, identified by the 'RA-AA00' references, established the model's core design and specifications. A second generation, often called the 'Kamasu II' ('RA-AA08' references), was later introduced, primarily distinguished by updated dials with gradient finishes. The entire Kamasu line has consistently utilized the in-house Orient Calibre F6922, which provides hacking and hand-winding capabilities.
